chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), he said:
You should say when you intend to sleep: 'O Allah, if You are to withhold my soul, then have mercy on it, and if You are to send it back, then protect it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite before sleeping in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this supplication encapsulates the Shia concept of *al-amr al-mu’allaq* (suspended decree) at the threshold of sleep, where the soul is temporarily released. It serves as a practical reminder of mortality, asking Allah to either grant mercy if death occurs or preserve health if life continues, thereby fostering constant spiritual awareness (*muraqabah*).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his fataher, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, raising it,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be saying whenever you intend to sleep, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If You<sup>azwj</sup> are to Withhold my soul so be Merciful to it, and if You<sup>azwj</sup> are to Send it (back to me), so Protect it’’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain individuals of his people in a marfu ’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said
the following: “When you are about to sleep say, ‘O Lord, if You holdback my soul from returning to my body, have mercy on it and if You will allow it to return, please protect it. ’”
